subject: Competitive eval / model quality follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: John Doe <john.doe@acme-payments.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 24 Jun 2026 23:05:00 -0700
Subject: Competitive eval / model quality follow-up

Hi John,

Thanks again for running the initial evaluation with your payments support prompts yesterday. I pulled together a short summary of the preliminary results and a proposed next steps list so we can move from qualitative impressions to repeatable regression checks. Attachments: acme_eval_results_v1.csv (raw outputs), redwood_vs_hyperscaler_slide.pdf (summary).

Top-level takeaways (preliminary):
- Redwood served-model (r-infer-v2) vs Hyperscaler-A endpoint:
  - Overall pass rate on sanity prompts: 93% vs 90%
  - Hallucination rate (factual hallucinations on verification set): 1.8% vs 3.6%
  - Cost per 1k tokens (your traffic mix): estimated 22% lower on Redwood with batching+cache
- Failure modes we saw: longer-context invoice interpretation sometimes dropped line-item totals (we've isolated to prompts #17-#23).

Proposed next tests (short-term):
1) Regression set A: 500 prompts (existing + edge cases) — we want exact-match and hallucination tagging.
2) Prompt sensitivity: run temperature sweep (0.0, 0.2, 0.7) on the top 50 edge prompts.
3) KV prefix caching test: rerun a sample of high-repeat customer prompts to validate token savings and latency impact.
4) Safety/hallucination audit: run the verification set under the same conditions you used for Hyperscaler-A and return detailed diff.

Can you confirm who on your side will own running Regression set A vs if you'd like Redwood to run it in our sandbox? If you want us to run it, we'll need the original customer-supplied prompts and the expected answers (even if redacted).

Suggested times for a 30-min follow-up to align on the regression definition: Thu Jun 25 9:00-9:30am PT or 11:00-11:30am PT. If neither works, propose alternatives.

Thanks — short and actionable is best here.

—
Marissa Cole
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0182

Thanks for the clear summary and the files. Quick clarifications:
- We did the Hyperscaler-A runs with temperature 0.2 and a 2k token cap; happy to rerun with the exact temps you listed.
- We can run Regression set A on our infra but would prefer Redwood to run the standard diff tooling if you can (faster for us).
- Owner here will be me + Sara (cc'd on eval@). I'll upload the redacted expected answers to a shared folder unless you'd prefer we share via the sandbox you referenced.

Marissa / Neha —

Thanks, this is helpful. Action items on our side if Redwood will run the regression + diffs:
- Engineering: spin up r-infer-v2 and r-infer-v2-quant (8-bit) runs with temps [0.0,0.2,0.7] and the same token caps used by Acme. Track per-prompt latency and token counts.
- Evals team: add automated hallucination tagging (we'll use the existing fact-checker harness) and calculate hallucination rate + confidence intervals.
- DX/PM: prepare a short doc that defines "exact match" vs "semantic accept" for Acme's expected answers (so we can reproduce).
- Sales: confirm SSO/sandbox access and request the redacted expected answers link from John during the call.

I'll own the infra runs and should have first-pass diffs by EOD Friday (Jun 26). Neha — can you schedule the 11:00am PT meeting and include the sandbox link?
